name: TB6612FNG dual DC motor driver
description: Toshiba TB6612FNG dual H-bridge with low-resistance MOSFET outputs (0.5 Ohm upper+lower): runs two DC motors (or one bipolar stepper) clockwise, counter-clockwise, short-braked or coasting, 1.2 A average / 3.2 A peak per channel, PWM speed up to 100 kHz, from 2.7-5.5 V logic and a 2.5-13.5 V motor supply. Thermal shutdown, under-voltage lockout and a standby pin. Sold as: SparkFun Motor Driver - Dual TB6612FNG (1A), ROB-14450 (ROB-14451 with headers), 16 pins in two rows: GND B01 B02 A02 A01 GND VCC VM | PWMA AIN2 AIN1 STBY BIN1 BIN2 PWMB GND (the 2nd and 3rd GND are named GND2/GND3 here); also cloned as generic purple/red TB6612FNG modules with the same labels.
eli5: Lets your board make two small motors spin forwards or backwards at any speed, using a battery for the motor power.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (all GND pins are joined on the board): common to the motor supply and the microcontroller

pins.name: B01
pins.description: Motor B output 1 (BO1); connect the motor, never the microcontroller

pins.name: A01
pins.description: Motor A output 1 (AO1); connect the motor, never the microcontroller

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Second GND pin (printed GND on the board; joined to the other GND pins)

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Logic supply 2.7-5.5 V: use the microcontroller's 3.3 V so its GPIO highs reach 0.7 x VCC

pins.name: VM
pins.description: Motor supply 2.5-13.5 V (15 V absolute max); a 4xAA pack or 2S LiPo is typical. Use 4.5 V or more for the full 1.2 A per channel

pins.name: PWMA
pins.description: Channel A PWM speed input (high = drive, low = short brake); 200 kOhm pull-down inside; up to 100 kHz

pins.name: AIN2
pins.description: Channel A direction input 2 (200 kOhm pull-down inside)

pins.name: AIN1
pins.description: Channel A direction input 1 (200 kOhm pull-down inside)

pins.name: STBY
pins.description: Standby, shared by both channels: low = everything off; must be driven (or tied to VCC) high to run. 200 kOhm pull-down inside

pins.name: BIN1
pins.description: Channel B direction input 1 (200 kOhm pull-down inside)

pins.name: BIN2
pins.description: Channel B direction input 2 (200 kOhm pull-down inside)

pins.name: PWMB
pins.description: Channel B PWM speed input (200 kOhm pull-down inside)

pins.name: GND3
pins.description: Third GND pin (printed GND on the board; joined to the other GND pins)

buildNotes: Truth table (Toshiba datasheet): STBY high, then IN1 high/IN2 low = CW, IN1 low/IN2 high = CCW, IN1 = IN2 = high = short brake, IN1 = IN2 = low = stop (outputs off, motor coasts). PWM low with a direction set = short brake, so PWM sets the speed.
STBY, PWMx and the IN pins have 200 kOhm pull-downs inside: with STBY or PWMA unconnected the motor never turns. Drive STBY from a GPIO or tie it to VCC.
VCC is the logic supply (2.7-5.5 V): power it from the same 3.3 V as an ESP32/Pico, because an input counts as high only above 0.7 x VCC (3.85 V on a 5.5 V VCC).
VM is the motor supply, 2.5-13.5 V (absolute max 15 V). Small motors can run from USB 5 V; anything larger needs its own battery, with its minus joined to GND.
Per channel: 1.2 A average, 3.2 A peak for 10 ms; with VM below 4.5 V only 0.4 A. The SparkFun board has no heatsink and the chip shuts down at about 175 C.
Connect motors to A01/A02 and B01/B02 only; never wire a motor output to a GPIO.
The board already has the 0.1 uF and 10 uF supply capacitors; add a 100 uF electrolytic across VM-GND for motors with long leads.

driver.code:
# TB6612FNG dual DC motor driver (Toshiba), MicroPython driver for ONE channel (one DC motor).
# Make one TB6612FNG object per motor: channel A = AIN1, AIN2, PWMA; channel B = BIN1, BIN2, PWMB.
# Both channels share STBY: pass the same STBY pin to both, or tie STBY to VCC on the board.
# H-SW control function (Toshiba datasheet, page 4), STBY = H:
#   IN1 = H, IN2 = L, PWM = H -> CW   (OUT1 = H, OUT2 = L)
#   IN1 = L, IN2 = H, PWM = H -> CCW  (OUT1 = L, OUT2 = H)
#   IN1 = H, IN2 = H          -> short brake (OUT1 = OUT2 = L)
#   IN1 or IN2 high, PWM = L  -> short brake (so PWM gives "drive / brake" speed control)
#   IN1 = L, IN2 = L, PWM = H -> stop: outputs off (high impedance), motor coasts
#   STBY = L                  -> standby: outputs off, < 1 uA supply current
# Every input (IN1, IN2, PWM, STBY) has an internal 200 kOhm pull-down, so the motor is off while
# the GPIOs float. Input high >= 0.7 x VCC: run VCC from the same 3.3 V as the microcontroller.
# PWM frequency: up to 100 kHz (datasheet fPWM max); 20 kHz is above hearing range.
from machine import Pin, PWM


class TB6612FNG:
    def __init__(self, in1, in2, pwm, stby=None, freq=20000):
        """in1, in2, pwm: GPIO numbers of AIN1/AIN2/PWMA (or BIN1/BIN2/PWMB).
        stby: GPIO number wired to STBY, or None if STBY is tied to VCC."""
        self.in1 = Pin(in1, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.in2 = Pin(in2, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.pwm = PWM(Pin(pwm), freq=min(freq, 100000), duty_u16=0)
        self.stby = Pin(stby, Pin.OUT, value=1) if stby is not None else None

    def wake(self):
        """Leave standby (STBY high)."""
        if self.stby is not None:
            self.stby.value(1)

    def standby(self):
        """Standby (STBY low): both channels off, chip draws < 1 uA. Shared by channels A and B."""
        if self.stby is not None:
            self.stby.value(0)

    def drive(self, speed):
        """speed -100..100 %: positive = CW (OUT1 high), negative = CCW (OUT2 high), 0 = stop (coast)."""
        speed = max(-100, min(100, int(speed)))
        if speed == 0:
            self.stop()
            return
        self.wake()
        # Set direction first, then duty: PWM low phases give short brake, high phases drive.
        if speed > 0:
            self.in2.value(0)
            self.in1.value(1)
        else:
            self.in1.value(0)
            self.in2.value(1)
        self.pwm.duty_u16(abs(speed) * 65535 // 100)

    def forward(self, speed=100):
        self.drive(abs(speed))

    def reverse(self, speed=100):
        self.drive(-abs(speed))

    def brake(self):
        """Short brake: IN1 = IN2 = H (outputs both low, motor stops quickly)."""
        self.wake()
        self.in1.value(1)
        self.in2.value(1)
        self.pwm.duty_u16(65535)

    def stop(self):
        """Stop: IN1 = IN2 = L with PWM high, outputs high impedance, motor coasts."""
        self.in1.value(0)
        self.in2.value(0)
        self.pwm.duty_u16(65535)

example.code:
import time
from tb6612fng import TB6612FNG

# Motor A on AIN1/AIN2/PWMA, STBY driven by a GPIO.
motor = TB6612FNG({AIN1}, {AIN2}, {PWMA}, stby={STBY})
while True:
    motor.forward(75)
    print('motor A forward 75%')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.stop()
    print('motor A stopped')
    time.sleep(1)
